Subject: OrthoSys POC - SLA tolerances and remedies

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Redwood integration looks promising for our imaging transcription pipeline. We have one outstanding objection from IT and procurement: our internal ops team requires a temporary reduction in the uptime target for the POC environment from 99.95% to 99.5% for the first 90 days, paired with a firm cap on monthly service credits. Procurement is concerned about an open-ended credit liability during a pilot.

Specific asks:
- Uptime target during POC window: 99.5%
- Cap total monthly service credits at 15% of POC spend
- Limited termination right if production readiness is not met after pilot (30-day notice)

Can Redwood agree to the above while we pilot? We’re prepared to sign an MSA amendment if legal approves. Attaching our preferred MAP.

Thanks,
Daniel
Principal Product Manager
OrthoSys

Subject: Fwd: OrthoSys POC - SLA tolerances and remedies (exec approval request)

Team — forwarding Daniel’s ask (see original below). Summary and recommendation for Deal Desk / Exec approval:

Summary: OrthoSys (POC deal OR-2027-1483) requests a temporary SLO change for the pilot: lower uptime SLO to 99.5% for 90 days, cap monthly service credits at 15% of POC spend, and allow a 30‑day termination right post-pilot if production readiness is not met. They will sign an MSA amendment and want telemetry access during the pilot.

Commercial impact: POC $30k/mo run rate. Latency/uptime variance increases blocking risk but limited in time. If we accept open-ended credits the financial exposure could be material, so we should limit the cap and add operational guardrails.

Recommended terms for approval:
- Temporary SLO: 99.5% for a 90-day pilot window (explicit start/end dates in amendment).
- Service credit cap: 15% of the monthly POC invoice, absolute cap (no stacking) — after cap, Redwood liability extinguished for that month.
- One-time pilot discount: 10% off for the 90-day pilot (to offset reduced SLO).
- Operational obligations: OrthoSys provides SRE access to logs (read-only) and agrees to a joint incident review cadence.
- Termination: 30-day termination right without penalty during pilot; if terminated for cause due to Redwood non-conformance, OrthoSys may request a pro-rated credit only up to the 15% cap.
- Legal: modify MSA to add explicit cap and pilot window; include mutual cooperation clause and no other SLA waivers.

Ask: Marissa + Marcus — do you approve the commercial concession (10% pilot discount + 15% cap) and the SLO variance for 90 days? Jonas — any legal redlines that would block (we want to retain standard remedy structure and cap liability).

I’ve attached the redline template for quick reference.

Thanks,
Priyom

Attachment: sla-redline-orthosys.pdf (pdf redline)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: OrthoSys POC - SLA tolerances and remedies (exec approval request)

Thanks for the clear summary, Priyom. I’m comfortable approving the commercial concession on the following conditions:

1) Finance (Marcus) signs off on the one-time 10% pilot discount and confirms we accept the resulting revenue recognition treatment.
2) Legal (Jonas) confirms the amendment preserves Redwood’s standard indemnities and does not create a precedent for broader SLO relaxations.
3) Product/EngOps must document the operational runbook and validate that telemetry access (read-only) does not expose internal PII.

Marcus — can you confirm finance approval? Jonas — please provide any mandatory redline language; if you can greenlight the amendment in principle I’ll send the formal approval to Priyom to finalize with the customer.

— Marissa
VP, Sales Operations
